extracted.intended_audience: startup founders and PR/communications professionals preparing award-announcement press releases
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and a template for writing press releases announcing that a company or person has won an award, including when to issue press and how to structure headline, lede, body, boilerplate, multimedia, and distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industry-recognized credible body
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The awarding organization should be credible and recognized within the industry; this is a core condition for issuing press. Cite the awarding body's reputation when describing the award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competitive selection process
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The award should be given via a competitive process (not automatic or trivial). Explain the selection mechanics to demonstrate selectivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive evaluation criteria
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The award should be based on clear, substantive criteria (not vague or purely promotional). Describe what was evaluated to justify the announcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industry/regional/national prominence
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the scope and prominence of the award (industry, regional, national) when deciding whether to pursue press and how broadly to distribute the release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple-year recognition pattern
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awards that show a pattern of recognition over multiple years strengthen credibility; mention repeat honors to demonstrate ongoing merit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not promote pay-to-play awards
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid issuing press for awards that are essentially pay-to-play or bought recognitions; these undermine credibility and are listed as awards that don't warrant press.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid vanity recognition
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not treat vanity awards as press-worthy. If an award lacks independent vetting or significance, skip publicizing it broadly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not announce minor niche awards indiscriminately
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Very small or hyper-niche awards may not merit press; evaluate whether the audience and outlets care before issuing a release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid awards with thousands of winners
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awards that list thousands of winners dilute significance; such awards generally don't justify a press release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid self-nominated lists
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Self-nominated or self-submitted lists (without independent vetting) are poor candidates for press; they weaken credibility if publicized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headline format
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a concise, factual headline that names the winner, the award, and the year or category. Keep it clear and newsy rather than promotional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lede must state award, awarding body, and basis for award
rubrics_metrics.description: "[Company] has been named [Award] by [Awarding Body], recognizing [specific basis for the award]. The award honors [criteria], and [Company] was selected from [number] nominees."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open with who won, who awarded it, and why (specific basis or accomplishments). Include the award's criteria and the level of selectivity (number of nominees) to establish context and credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: About the Award paragraph
rubrics_metrics.description: Para 1: About the Award — Awarding organization credibility; Selection process; Criteria; Number of nominees / selectivity
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain the award: who runs it, how winners are chosen, what criteria are used, and how selective it is. These details justify the newsworthiness of the honor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Why [Company] Won paragraph
rubrics_metrics.description: Para 2: Why [Company] Won — Specific accomplishments cited; Years of qualifying work; Customer/community impact; Industry recognition
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List concrete accomplishments and metrics that led to the award (projects, milestones, years of work, customer outcomes). Focus on evidence rather than vague praise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quote guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Para 3: Quote — From CEO or senior executive; Honors team and customers; Acknowledges the awarding body; Honest about ongoing work
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a substantive, authentic quote from a senior leader that thanks the team/customers, acknowledges the awarding body, and situates the honor in ongoing efforts—avoid canned or self-congratulatory language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other recognition paragraph
rubrics_metrics.description: Para 4: Other Recognition — Brief mention of other recent recognition; Pattern of credibility
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicable, mention other recent awards or recognitions to show a pattern of external validation; keep this brief and relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boilerplate content
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard company description — Mission and scale; Geographic reach
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a short, standardized company boilerplate covering mission, scale, and geographic footprint. Keep it consistent with other corporate materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multimedia inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Award trophy/certificate image; Award ceremony photos; CEO accepting if applicable; Customer/team work photos
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide high-quality images (trophy, ceremony, executive accepting, team or customer work) to increase pickup and engagement. Attach or link assets for reporters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Local press for regional awards; Industry publications for sector awards; National press only for major recognition; Wire syndication for SEO; LinkedIn announcement from CEO and team
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match distribution to the award's scope: pitch local outlets for regional honors, trade press for sector-specific awards, national outlets only for broadly significant recognitions. Use wire services for SEO and encourage company leaders to post on LinkedIn.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality Rubric for Awards (summary)
rubrics_metrics.description: Award is from credible body; Selection process described; Specific accomplishments cited; Substantive CEO quote; Multimedia included; Distribution matches award scope; Honest about competitive context
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this short checklist to assess whether an award merits a press release: ensure the awarding body is credible, the selection process is transparent, the release names concrete accomplishments, includes a meaningful executive quote and multimedia, matches distribution to scope, and candidly describes the competitive context.
